component: P16 caller trust-floor lifecycle counterexample tests
constraints: Execute two fixed caller-argument traces against the actual stateless verifier, using actual synthetic signatures. No storage, restart, network or controller is involved.
Retain both the unsafe caller replay outcome and the protected outcome; rejected statements must not provide trusted metadata or authority.
alternatives: Python unittest direct API traces with scoped function replacement for sensitivity controls.
TLA+ with TLC for a state-transition specification and bounded model exploration.
Alloy relational/temporal models with Analyzer counterexample search.
Erlang PropEr model-based generated stateful test sequences.
Java/Kotlin JUnit orchestration of the actual library through an explicit process boundary.
rationale: KEEP the direct executable traces: they inspect the exact verifier and its returned metadata, rather than a separately encoded model. Two existing traces and eight policy methods pass alongside one lexical method.

TLA+ and Alloy are strong candidates for exploring a future persistent/concurrent state lifecycle; neither model alone establishes behavior of these Python calls. PropEr offers generated stateful tests, while these two traces are fixed regression counterexamples.

JUnit can drive an adapter, but the adapter adds a representation boundary without a demonstrated benefit for these fixed direct calls. No deadline, throughput or target memory budget motivates a native test-driver migration.

Two sensitivity experiments replace only a supplied floor argument before invoking the real verifier. Each causes one expected assertion failure with no errors/skips; original bindings are restored. No new implementation mismatch is demonstrated.
limits: KEEP concerns the two test traces, not a storage technology choice or exemption for future persistent state.
Policy enrollment, authenticated configuration delivery, clock trust and durable anti-rollback state are not implemented by these tests.
Alternative tools were researched, not benchmarked or used for model checking. No language performance ranking or formal proof is claimed.
No hardware, tactical, MLS/CNSA, availability, installed-product or whole-lane qualification.
